system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: Two domain logons for leo.martins failed with bad-password status from 203.0.113.250, followed about 72 seconds later by a successful network logon for the same account from that same address.

The successful network logon was recorded on the domain controller with Kerberos and LogonType 3; its source address is not among the listed organization hosts or the 10.40.10.23 address later seen in authentication records.

Given the preceding bad-password attempts, the successful logon from an unlisted source address, and the stated absence of VPN access, the authentication sequence is suspicious and supports an unauthorized-access finding.

Dropbox started in leo.martins's workstation session, and a later proxy record shows that account connecting to ca.slack-edge.com; the supplied approved-services context does not list Dropbox or Slack as approved.

A subsequent interactive logon on WS-LMARTINS-01 was followed by ordinary user-session startup and a webpack process launched from the clinical-portal repository; this does not establish that the earlier network logon was authorized.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records do not identify who controlled source address 203.0.113.250 or provide attribution, location, or device details for it.
The proxy evidence is a single CONNECT record and does not show the contents transferred, the user’s intent, or whether data was uploaded.
The available records do not show what actions, if any, followed the successful network logon from 203.0.113.250.
claims_not_established: The identity of the person or device that made the failed and successful logon attempts.
Whether the successful logon from 203.0.113.250 was authorized or resulted in access to data or systems.
Whether Dropbox or the Slack connection was used to transfer organizational data.
Whether the later interactive session on WS-LMARTINS-01 was related to the earlier network logon.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate 203.0.113.250 with firewall, DHCP, endpoint, and network-flow records to identify its source and any related connections.
Review domain-controller and target-host logs around the successful network logon for accessed services, subsequent authentication, and actions under leo.martins.
Check endpoint telemetry for Dropbox sync activity, files accessed or transferred, and the process or user activity associated with the Slack connection.
Confirm with leo.martins and IT whether the logons and the Dropbox/Slack activity were expected.
